title: Asymmetric Bubble Coalescence on Biphilic Surfaces in Nucleate Boiling: Suppressed Jumping and Advanced Departure
content: Coalescence of neighboring bubbles is common in nucleate boiling, yet its dynamics on biphilic surfaces remain insufficiently understood. Here, the growth, coalescence and departure of two bubbles on a biphilic surface with two hydrophobic spots were investigated by three-dimensional volume-of-fluid simulations validated against pool boiling experiments. The activation time of the second bubble was varied over the whole growth period of the first bubble. Five modes were identified: symmetric, early-stage, late-stage and departure-stage coalescence, and non-coalescence. In early-stage coalescence, the departure time is nearly independent of the activation time, whereas in late-stage coalescence it increases almost linearly with the activation time, and the transition between the two regimes is abrupt. Compared with a single bubble, departure is advanced by up to 34\%. Coalescence-induced jumping does not occur, because the contact lines pinned at the spot edges raise the adhesion energy far above the jumping threshold. Departure is instead governed by buoyancy acting against this pinning. In late-stage coalescence, the Laplace pressure difference releases the smaller bubble from its spot, so that the coalesced bubble, held by a single spot, departs much earlier. These results show that the activation timing of neighboring hydrophobic spots can advance bubble departure on biphilic surfaces.
